messages:
nina.design: quick sync 1 thinking about an explicit speedbump pattern for canary increases + how the timeline toggle should behave for longer histories. sketch: https://figma.redwood/canary-speedbump-v2. main asks: confirm modal microcopy, slider affordances, a11y announcements, and timeline collapse behavior.
omar_pm: short 1 we need a mandatory confirmation for any change >25% and an additional typed confirmation for >75%. last week someone slid to 90% on accident. :grimacing:
raul.eng: implementation notes: slider snaps at 1% increments <10%, 5% increments 10-50%, 10% increments >50%. typed-confirmation requires exact variant name match. we can also add an API gate that rejects programmatic changes above the typed-confirm threshold unless the request includes a signed audit token.
claire_a11y: a11y checklist: 1) modal must announce role=dialog with aria-modal and clear H1. 2) Confirm button must include numeric percent and variant name, e.g., "Confirm: route 75% to v2-rc". 3) Add aria-live="polite" region that reports "Allocation set to 75% for v2-rc" after change. 4) contrast: traffic bar midtone currently 3.0:1; legends at small size need 4.5:1. consider using pattern fills for the bands too.
tess_research: in unmoderated tests participants misread the tiny timestamp ticks when there are >8 versions. They also expected an audit trail link right on the modal ("why did this change happen?"). preference leaned toward a more readable timeline by default.
nina.design: microcopy draft for the modal: "Confirm rollout increase
You are about to route 75% of live traffic to variant \u2018v2-rc\u2019. This change will expose more users to the variant. Ensure monitoring and rollback plan are ready. Type \u2018v2-rc\u2019 to confirm." open to tone adjustments 1 is "expose" ok?
omar_pm: prefer to avoid jargon 1 maybe: "This will send 75% of users to the variant and may increase error rates. Confirm to proceed." include quick checklist: [x] monitoring, [ ] rollback tested, [ ] alerts configured. capture free-text reason.
raul.eng: +1 capture reason. also add optional toggle: "Enable auto-rollback (5min window)". backend supports metric-based triggers; we'll wire it to the existing alert rules. also, if typed confirmation is required, we should reject API calls that don't include the typed_confirmation field to avoid accidental scripts.
claire_a11y: button label recommendation: "Increase to 75%: v2-rc". explicit, short, numeric. ensure focus moves to the cancel button first (safety) then to confirm on a deliberate tab.
tess_research: timeline UX: default to expanded list (one row per version) up to 8 items, then collapse older entries into an "Archived history" grouped row with a toggle to expand. users liked the grouped summary + a clear "Show more" affordance. also add a vertical time marker on hover or keyboard focus.
nina.design: good call. keyboard shortcut idea: press `t` to toggle compact/expanded timeline. need discoverability hint near the control.
omar_pm: product note: default to expanded for auditability, compact toggle for power users. logging: always record actor, percent, reason, whether typed confirmation was used, and whether auto-rollback was enabled.
raul.eng: perf note: rendering many SVG bands is heavy. we'll implement virtualization and an aggregated bucket for >20 historical versions. UX will show an ellipsis band for aggregated history.
nina.design: copy alternatives for CTA: "Confirm: Increase to 75%", "Start canary", "Apply allocation". which is clearest?
claire_a11y: "Increase to 75%: v2-rc" wins for screen readers and accessibility. avoids verbs like "start" which are ambiguous. include percent numeric.
omar_pm: +1. also add a small inline footer note: "This change is immediate. Notifications will be sent to #deployments and on-call."
tess_research: micro-interaction: after confirm, show a transient toast with an action link "View audit" which takes you to the change log for that rollout. users expect immediate access to context.
raul.eng: we'll emit an event to the audit service and include a deep link in the toast. API clients get the audit id in the response.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary increased by omar_pm 1 v2-rc to 75% (auto-rollback=true) 1 2025-05-12T14:30:00Z
nina.design: thanks everyone 1 I'll update the figma with the typed-confirm flow, CTA label, timeline grouping rules, and accessibility notes. planning a quick review at 11am PT tomorrow
